newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand to cut 450 annual job equivalent.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand to cut 450 annual job equivalent.

text.p: Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA said on Friday it planned to cut about 450 annual job equivalents through natural wastage.
"There is a clear goal to carry out this without firing people," the statement said.
The measure, planned to take place next year, corresponds to a cut of about 10 percent, a company spokeswoman said.
Storebrand has about 4,050 annual job equivalents, distributed among 4,200 employees.
The effect of the accounts, including provisions, will be recorded in the third quarter this year, the statement said.
The company will present nine-month results on November 6.
The statement followed an announcement in August by chief executive officer Age Korsvold that competition in the insurance industry called for better cost effectiveness throughout the group.
The company's first half operating profit was 2.76 billion crowns before the distribution to life policy-holders, 766 million crowns higher than in the January-June period 1995.
Korsvold has also called on staff to propose ways of cutting costs by 40 percent in each unit of the group, although he made clear not all of the proposals may be implemented.
